title: Microinteraction timeline: token-driven theme, non-modal tooltips, and keyboard scrubbing that avoids reflow
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Our time-series micro-interactions (hover scrubbing, keyboard scrubbing, and point tooltips) currently cause layout reflows and have inconsistent behavior across themes and high-density datasets. On mobile/low-power devices and in private deployments we see jank and elevated CPU usage. Goal: define a token-driven implementation and interaction pattern that is accessible, minimizes main-thread layout work, supports high-density fallback rendering, and provides a consistent look across tokens (light/dark/brand).

Scope: design tokens mapping for chart micro-states (hover, active, focus), a non-modal tooltip pattern that avoids blocking keyboard focus, keyboard-first scrubbing semantics, and recommendations for canvas/SVG hybrid rendering to reduce reflow. Deliverables: Figma prototypes (desktop + mobile), spec doc with token names and examples, keyboard interaction spec, acceptance criteria, and a small Storybook story demonstrating perf vs baseline.

Design constraints and assumptions: use CSS tokens already defined in the design system (color, elevation, radius, motion-duration). Charts may be rendered via canvas for heavy series; we must provide a pattern that works for both DOM (SVG/HTML overlay) and canvas renderers. Accessibility must meet WCAG 2.2 AA and keyboard users must be able to scrub without losing context or encountering modal traps.
acceptance_criteria: Tooltip: non-modal pattern implemented so tooltips do not steal focus — role/relationship uses aria-describedby or aria-owns and does not change document focus
Keyboard scrubbing: left/right arrow moves the scrub position; scrubbing announces point summary via an accessible status region without causing layout shifts
Token-driven visuals: chart micro-state token names documented (chart.hover-bg, chart.hover-outline, chart.focus-ring, chart.tooltip-bg) and examples in Figma
Performance: 95th percentile tooltip open + update action under 40ms on modern desktop; on low-power device CPU budget for chart micro-interactions reduced by at least 30% vs current baseline
Fallbacks: OffscreenCanvas usage recommended for Dedicated/Private deployments with CPU profiling notes; clear SVG/DOM fallback guidance for environments without worker support
QA: Storybook entries for Desktop, Mobile, High-density dataset; automated accessibility checklist and keyboard e2e test recorded
comments: 2026-02-20 Ava Martinez: Created ticket after pairing with Eng to reproduce jank on a dense dataset. Captured session in Loom (link below). Proposed pattern: move hover indicator using CSS transform on an overlay element to avoid reflow, render points as canvas layer for heavy datasets.

2026-02-24 Samir Rao: Eng notes — agree on transform-based indicator. Will prototype an overlay that only updates transform/opacity. We should measure paint costs of overlay vs drawing a small indicator on the canvas to avoid double-rendering in heavy paths.

2026-02-28 Design review: Iterated Figma demo with token mappings. Decisions: (1) Tooltip anchor uses absolute positioned overlay with pointer-events: none on the chart canvas to reduce hit-test costs; (2) Tooltip content popper is non-modal and connected via aria-describedby to the focused element; (3) Provide an off-screen aria-live status for keyboard scrub announcements instead of focusing the tooltip.

2026-03-03 Eng prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ui/pull/1592 — implements transform-based hover indicator and an OffscreenCanvas path. Early perf delta: 25% CPU reduction on a 16-series test trace, tooltip latency ~32ms median. Asked for design token naming confirmation.

2026-03-06 Accessibility feedback from Priya Kapoor: Use role='status' for live region with aria-atomic='true' to announce scrub changes; ensure we do not announce every millisecond during fast scrubs — debounce to 120ms. Also verify that screen readers ignore the moving overlay element when not focused.

2026-03-10 PM review (Jonah Liu): Add acceptance criteria for Storybook stories and add a small user-study with 5 power-users to validate discoverability of keyboard scrubbing. Also requested to capture telemetry flags to evaluate adoption.

2026-03-12 Samir Rao: Updated prototype to debounce announcements and added canvas-indicator fallback. Preparing a performance test matrix to validate 95th percentile under 40ms across target regions. Next: finalize token names and submit design-spec PR.
